en: The Apadāna of the Elder Padumakūṭāgāriya Pilindavaccha Chapter, Number 5 I was once a householder in the city of Benares, A wealthy man, possessing great riches and grain. At that time, the Buddha, the Teacher, the One with Vision, The All-Knowing, the All-Seeing, appeared in the world. Having renounced the household life for homelessness, He dwelt at Isipatana near Varanasi. Then, having heard of the appearance of the Buddha, I went to see the Teacher, the One with Vision. Having approached the Blessed One, the One with Vision, I paid homage to him and sat down to one side. As I sat there, the Blessed One, the One with Vision, Out of compassion for me, taught the Dhamma. Having heard the Dhamma from the Blessed One, the One with Vision, I attained the fruit of stream-entry (*sotāpatti-phala*). Then, having taken refuge in the Triple Gem, And having undertaken the five precepts, I offered a lotus-stalked gabled hut To the Blessed One, the One with Vision. Because of that wholesome deed, For eighty-four thousand aeons, I never fell into the lower realms; I was always reborn in the heavenly worlds. In my final existence here on earth, I was born into a family of great wealth. When I was twenty years of age, I went forth into homelessness under the Buddha Kassapa. Having practiced the holy life under the Teacher Kassapa, I was reborn in the Brahma-world after death. From that Brahma-world, when my lifespan ended, I was reborn in this human world. Now, as a monk, I have attained the fruit of Arhatship; My mind is liberated, free from all taints. I have lived the holy life; what was to be done has been done; There is no further state of existence for me beyond this. Thus did the Elder Padumakūṭāgāriya speak his own history. May it be well. “The Blessed One named Piyadassī,
the self-become leader of the world,
the perfectly awakened one who desires solitude.”
The Sage skilled in concentration,
the Great Sage Piyadassi, having entered a forest grove;
Having spread out a rag-robe,
the Supreme Person sat down;
formerly, I was a deer-hunter.
In a forest grove,
seeking deer,
I was wandering about at that time.
There I saw the Fully Awakened One,
who had crossed over the flood and was free from taints,
like a blossoming king of sal trees.
Having seen the God of Gods, who is as radiant as the risen sun,
lovely to behold and of great glory;
Having plunged into the Jātassara lake,
I then brought forth a lotus.
Having brought forth that lotus, I—
Having constructed a delightful gabled chamber with a hundred petals,
I covered it with a lotus.
Compassionate, merciful,
lovely to behold, the Great Sage;
for seven days and nights, the Buddha—
The Conqueror dwelt in the gabled hall.
Having discarded the old,
I covered it with new.
Having raised my hands in añjali,
I stood there for some time. Then,
having emerged from that meditative concentration, I remained.
The Great Sage Piyaḍassī,
the Leader of the World, sat down while surveying the directions.
At that time, there was an attendant named Sudassana,
possessed of great psychic power;
having understood the Buddha’s mind, he—
Of the Teacher Piyadassi,
surrounded by a retinue of eighty thousand bhikkhus.
He approached the Leader of the World as he sat happily at the edge of the forest,
throughout the entire woodland grove.
And the deities who inhabited them,
having understood the Buddha’s thought,
all assembled there at that time.
When the yakkhas had assembled,
along with the kumbhaṇḍas and rakkhasas,
and the community of bhikkhus had arrived.
The Jina uttered this verse:
“He who worshipped me for seven days and provided me with a dwelling;”
I shall proclaim that;
listen as I speak.
It is very difficult to see and exceedingly subtle.
Profound and well-expounded;
I shall praise it with wisdom—
listen as I speak.
For fourteen eons,
he will exercise sovereignty over the gods;
for one who is great, there is a peaked gabled palace.
Covered with lotus flowers,
it will be held up in the sky;
this is the fruit of that work of merit involving flowers.
For four hundred and twenty-four aeons,
he will wander through the cycle of existence.
There, he will dwell in a celestial mansion made of flowers.
He will hold it in the air,
just as water does not cling to a lotus leaf.
In the same way, no defilements cling to his knowledge;
having turned back the mind, [he abides].
Having abandoned these five hindrances,
he will generate a mind of renunciation and go forth from the home life.
Then, carrying a mansion made of flowers,
he will depart while dwelling at the foot of a tree.
For the one who is prudent and mindful,
a celestial palace made of flowers will be borne upon his head.
Having given robes, almsfood,
requisites, and lodgings to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus,
“...shall attain Nibbāna, free from taints.
While traveling in a gabled house,
I went forth into homelessness.
Even while dwelling at the foot of a tree,
a gabled house is provided;
likewise with robes and almsfood.
Volition does not exist for me;
being joined with meritorious action,
I obtain what is fully accomplished.
Counted by numbers,
many millions of aeons have passed for me—
empty ones indeed have they been.
The leaders of the world are liberated.
In eighteen hundred kappas,
Piyadassī will be the guide.
Having attended upon him,
I have come to this womb;
here I behold the Perfectly Awakened One.
The One with Vision named Anoma;
having approached him,
I went forth into the homeless life.
The Buddha, the Victor who brings an end to suffering, taught the path to me;
having heard his Dhamma, I...
I have attained the immovable state,
having satisfied the Fully Awakened One,
Gotama, the bull of the Śākyas.
Having fully understood all taints,
I dwell free from taints for eighteen hundred eons.
Because I worshipped the Buddha,
I do not know a state of misery;
this is the fruit of worshipping the Buddha.
The defilements have been incinerated by me;
all states of existence have been uprooted;
all taints are completely exhausted.
Now there is no further becoming.
Welcome indeed has come to me... [as before] ...
This is the teaching of the Buddha.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth].
“Such is the teaching of the Buddha.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Padumakūṭāgāriya speak these verses.
This is the fifth legend of the elder Padumakūṭāgāriya.
